pattern:
The full request is: $ARGUMENTS
The first token is the episode id ($setup.output); everything after it
is the premise.
replacement: The premise for this episode is in Episodes/{{episodeId}}/premise.md. Read it first; it is the request.
{{results.diff}} — the full diff is in Production/{{episodeId}}/canon-diff.patch; read that file, not this summary.

pattern:
After writing prompts.json, run the project's own guard against it and
fix anything it reports, then re-run until it prints 0:

  uv run python -c "
  import json, importlib.util
  s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('g', '.archon/scripts/nano-banana-generate.py')
  g = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s)
  try: s.loader.exec_module(g)
  except SystemExit: pass
  d = json.load(open('Production/$setup.output/images/prompts.json'))
  bad = [(x['id'], sorted(set(g.find_collective_populators(x.get('brief','')))))
         for x in d['shots'] if x.get('type') == 'character']
  bad = [b for b in bad if b[1]]
  print('POPULATOR VIOLATIONS:', len(bad))
  [print(' ', i, '->', ', '.join(h)) for i, h in bad]"

This is the same function the pipeline enforces minutes later, where a
single hit rejects the WHOLE run and every image goes ungenerated. Three
consecutive episodes have been halted this way, every time on innocent
wording. Catch it here, where it costs nothing.

End with: the shot count, ambient-vs-character split, the guard's
violation count (must be 0), and the list of character-shot ids +
one-line briefs (the Nano-Banana gate shows this to the showrunner).
replacement: The pipeline runs the collective-populator check (populator-check.py) after this step and stops the line if a brief describes a crowd without naming its members. Do not run Python yourself; write briefs that name every populator.
